summary: WebRender, Firefox’s GPU compositor, saw broad work to improve rendering quality and efficiency: it avoids redundant GPU uploads, refines antialiasing and clipping, and fixes issues affecting gradients, shadows, text, and video overlays. A major architectural effort separates WebRender’s rendering interface from OpenGL-specific details, making room for different GPU backends; developer tools also gained shader editing and reloading, scene inspection, and texture viewing features.
